name: Gajar Shorba
subtitle: Carrots cooked down with ginger and blended smooth, sweet against black pepper

ingredients.note: carries the whole dish against the sweetness
or oil, which makes it vegan
optional; a swirl, not a dose

prepNotes: Carrots are sweet and a sweet soup is dull, so the pepper and the ginger are not seasoning here, they are the other half of the dish. Be heavier with both than feels right.
Old winter carrots make a better shorba than young ones. They have less water and more sugar.

steps.text: Warm the butter and crackle the cumin. Add the onion, ginger and garlic and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Add the carrots, salt and water. Simmer covered 20-25 minutes, until a piece crushes against the side of the pan with no resistance.
steps.tip: Undercooked carrot will not blend smooth; it goes fibrous instead of silky.

steps.text: Blend until completely smooth, then pass through a sieve.
steps.tip: Carrot has enough fibre to stay slightly rough however good the blender. The sieve is what makes it a shorba.

steps.text: Return to the pan, thin to a pouring consistency with hot water, and add the cracked pepper. Simmer 2 minutes more so the pepper opens up.
Check the salt, swirl in the cream if using, and finish with coriander.
steps.tip: Taste before the cream. It rounds off the pepper, and if the pepper was too shy to begin with it will disappear altogether.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and freezes for a month without the cream, which is better stirred in on reheating.
